title: Jump Game VI
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> dp: n entries → O(n)
- deque<int> dq: up to k entries (bounded by n) → O(k)
- not counted: input nums, returned int
approach: Define dp[i] as the maximum score to reach index i. Then dp[i] = nums[i] + max(dp[j]) for j in [i-k, i-1]. A monotonic deque storing indices with decreasing dp values maintains the sliding window maximum in O(1) amortized per step: pop stale front indices outside the window, read the max from the front, then pop back indices whose dp value is ≤ the new dp[i] before pushing i. This gives O(n) time and O(n) space.
hints: At each position, you can arrive from any of the last k positions. With n and k both up to 10^5, what do you need to track about those k positions to avoid checking all of them at every step?
Use a monotonic deque storing indices with decreasing dp values. For nums = [1,-1,-2,4,-7,3], k = 2: at i = 3, the deque holds indices [1, 2] with dp values [0, -1], so dp[3] = 4 + 0 = 4.

```
dp[0] = nums[0]
deque = [0]
for i from 1 to n-1:
    remove front indices outside [i-k, i-1]
    dp[i] = nums[i] + dp[deque.front]
    remove back indices whose dp value <= dp[i]
    push i to back
return dp[n-1]
```

**Single element** - n = 1, the loop never executes
`Input: nums = [5], k = 1` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: returning dp[n-1] without initializing dp[0] = nums[0] first → returns 0

**All negative values** - every jump decreases the total score
`Input: nums = [-1,-2,-3], k = 2` → `Expected: -4`
⚠️ Bug: initializing dp[0] = 0 instead of nums[0] → returns -3

**Off-by-one window** - the boundary index i - k is still a valid jump source
`Input: nums = [5,-10,1], k = 2` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: using `dq.front() <= i - k` instead of `<` removes index 0 at i = 2 → returns -4

followUps.q: What if k varies per index, given as an array k[i]?
followUps.a: The same monotonic deque works. At index i, remove front indices where index < i - k[i]. The window size changes per index but the deque operations remain O(1) amortized. TC: O(n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if you must return the actual sequence of indices that achieves the maximum score?
followUps.a: Store a predecessor array prev[i] alongside dp[i]. When computing dp[i], record which index j gave the maximum. Reconstruct the path by following prev pointers backward from n-1 to 0. TC: O(n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a stream and cannot fit in memory?
followUps.a: Maintain a deque of size at most k and a circular buffer of the last k dp values. Process each element as it arrives, mapping index i to buffer slot i % k. Only the last k dp values and the deque need storage. TC: O(n), SC: O(k).
